newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Pound down versus mark, Euro bourses weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Pound down versus mark, Euro bourses weak.

text.p: Sterling fell back sharply against the mark in late European business on Thursday on profit-taking after Britain's central bank raised its base rate by a quarter percentage point to 6.75 percent.

Most European bourses, more focused on the British rate rise and earlier comments from German central bank members that sent the dollar lower, got only limited support from Wall Street's higher opening.
The Dow later slid into negative territory.
London stocks eventually edged up on relief that the Bank of England's (BOE) expected rate rise was only a quarter point instead of the half point some analysts had forecast.
But for SocGen strategist Andy Hartwill, the quarter- point rise came as no surprise.

"This was entirely expected as far as the equity market is concerned," said Hartwill. "Maybe we can sit back for a while and wait for these rises to take effect. The market will like it a damned sight more than 50 basis points."
Others said the smaller rate rise was disheartening because it made the central bank seem soft on inflation.
"I would have hoped that the Bank of England would roar but in fact it hasn't," said Richard Jeffrey, chief economist at Charterhouse.
"I think we will look back on these rate rises and conclude that (the BOE) was not aggressive enough...I think we'll eventually see the market come off."
Sterling and the dollar were already losing against the mark when the rate rise was announced because of earlier comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer.

The pound briefly recovered to 2.9750 marks from a low of 2.9513 hit just after the rate announcement as investors bought at the lows. But it just as quickly resumed its slide towards session lows, trading at 2.9570 in late Europe.
Against the dollar the pound ended around $1.6870 versus a previous late rate of $1.6842.

Tietmeyer said Germany's central bank was watching foreign exchange market developments closely and that the dollar's sharp rise against the mark was now over. At its peak, the dollar was up 14 percent against the mark this year.
"We will naturally watch the developments in markets," he said. "You can be sure that it is important for us that the mark remains a strong currency and we enter the euro as a strong currency."
The European Union's euro single currency is set to be launched on January 1, 1999.
The dollar slipped further against the mark after the Dutch central bank raised its special advances rate 0.10 point to 3.00 percent in the afternoon.
The Dutch rate increase was seen as reinforcing ideas that interest rates in Germany might have bottomed. Some traders closely watch action on the Dutch rate as a prelude to German moves.
More Tietmeyer comments, coupled with the dollar's fall, also pressured German shares, forcing the 30-share DAX to snap its streak of seven consecutive record high closes.
Tietmeyer said the DAX's surge did not reflect the health of the entire German economy.

Profit-taking in the DAX index also emerged as investors rushed to take profits after the Bundesbank said it was closely watching the DAX's recent sharp gains. The DAX scored a record high of 4,066.09 on Wednesday.
But traders expected the DAX's losses to be short-lived. "This appears to be a one-day reversal for now. But it may be time for some consolidation," a Frankfurt dealer said.

In Paris, paper and timber group La Rochette was the biggest winner. The share ended up 7.79 percent at 24.90 French francs, off its session high of 25.50, up 10 percent, when the stock was suspended for 15 minutes at its upper daily trading limit.
In metals markets, London gold ended little changed, consolidating its rise from 12-year lows.
Dealers expected gold prices to keep drifting up on Friday. "I think we have seen the lows, and the next move is toward $325," a dealer at a major Swiss bank said.
But traders said sentiment remained bearish and heavy selling could reemerge next week.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 113.05 yen and 1.7523 marks in late Europe compared with 112.97 and 1.7612 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 5.4 points at 4,767.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed bourse trading down 63.48 points at 3,992.38.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 21.47 points to 2,929.09.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $319.65 per ounce in London, compared with Wednesday's close of $319.75. Silver finished at $4.34, flat from Wednesday's close.
